preconditions: W: explicitly invoked guarded payload hashing in an active consumption window; owned temporary inputs. Allocation/read failures are labelled injections, not native host-quota or OOM measurements.
steps: Hash a real 32 MiB attachment with 64 KiB and 4 KiB reusable buffers; bind the complete byte count and independent incremental SHA-256.
Exercise smaller pre-read buffer allocation alternatives, short reads, exact control positions, guarded descriptor lifetime and unchanged critical fixture bytes on failure.

oracle.requirement_contract: Vor bekannten großen Speicher- und Stagingallokationen MUSS SpecRoad die sparsame Alternative und tatsächliche Verfügbarkeit nach Anhang O.3 prüfen.
oracle.scope: The actual bounded bytearray allocation is attempted before payload consumption; an injected allocation MemoryError halves the requested capacity down to one byte, with a finite stop if the minimum fails. A failure after input consumption is never silently retried. Actual reserved payload capacity is registered separately from measured RSS and released from active ownership on success/failure. A real owned 32 MiB file is read with one observed reusable buffer; tracemalloc bounds the selected Python allocation window below 2 MiB. Full-payload copy, claimed host quota, staging availability or whole-product completion is not inferred.

open_items: Partial bounded payload-hash driver only. Controlled host/resource-blocker projection, native memory/permission failures and indivisible minimum steps follow in 6.e.R. Archive/import/snapshot consumers, known-limit integration, staging capacity/reserves, persistent work and complete runtime/platform acceptance remain open. The measured Python allocation window is not total RSS or a host capacity guarantee.
